title: The Dawn of Voice AI Possibility
summary: Voice AI use cases by call type, from scheduling and intake to banking, insurance, collections and dispatch, with what each agent does and what breaks.
body_markdown:
A voice AI use case is a defined call type that a[voice agent](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/what-is-an-ai-voice-agent) handles end to end. It answers or places the call, collects what it needs, acts in a connected system and ends with a recorded outcome. Below are nine, with what the agent does on the call and what tends to break.


Use cases for voice AI agents tend to stall on multi-turn reliability. The agent handles the first turns of a call and loses it later, because errors compound across turns.[Our single-turn testing post](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/why-single-turn-testing-falls-short-in-evaluating-conversational-ai) works through the arithmetic. At 99% accuracy per turn, about one 10-turn call in ten contains an error, and at 95% only about 60% of 10-turn calls come out clean. The use cases that work in production are tested across the full call.


## Appointment scheduling and reminders


The agent takes a request to book, move or cancel, checks the calendar or practice system, writes the change and reads the confirmation back. Reminders run the same flow outbound.


Two things break. Conditional requests such as "move it to Tuesday if the weather clears" force the agent to hold a pending intent across turns, and a mid-call change of mind often leaves the old slot booked beside the new one. The other is the write itself: the agent says the slot is confirmed while the tool call created a duplicate or used the wrong time zone. Score the calendar entry the call produced. Our[test of five AI appointment booking tools](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/best-ai-appointment-booking-tools) covers how each handled accents, noise and mid-call changes.


## Patient intake and triage


The agent answers or places calls to collect symptoms, medications and insurance details, confirms identity, and routes the case to a queue or clinician.


Medical vocabulary and identity matching break first. A general STT model can hear "15 mg" as "50 mg", and patients describe symptoms in fragments with long pauses, so a VAD tuned for clean speech cuts them off and drops the detail that mattered. A wrong match to the patient record is worse, because the agent then writes to someone else's chart. Triage also needs a hard handoff rule: symptoms outside what the agent is cleared to assess go to a human, with scenarios of their own. The[guide to conversational AI in healthcare](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/conversational-ai-in-healthcare) covers EHR integration and these failure points.


## Inbound customer support and call deflection


The agent resolves the top call reasons against backend systems: order and account status, returns, plan changes. Anything it cannot close, it transfers.


Scope drift breaks it first: callers bring a billing dispute to a line built for order status, and an agent with no escalation path for unrecognized intents loops or guesses. The second is the handoff, where the transfer drops context and the caller repeats everything. Measurement breaks too, because a caller who hangs up in frustration looks like one who got an answer, and deflection rate overstates success. The[call deflection guide](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/call-deflection) works through HMRC's audited data: 12.3 million of 36.5 million calls in 2023-24 ended after a deflection message, and those callers reported 28% satisfaction against 63% for callers who reached an adviser.


## Virtual receptionist and call routing


The agent answers every inbound call, identifies the caller and the need, then routes to a person, takes a message, books a slot or logs a lead. It also covers after-hours and overflow calls that would otherwise reach voicemail.


Routing by name is the first weak point. Callers ask for someone by nickname, STT mangles proper names, and the agent transfers to the wrong extension with full confidence. The second is the transfer itself: what summary reaches the human, and whether the transfer completes when the target line is busy or the office is closed. Test each of those states. Our[test of nine AI receptionist tools](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/best-rated-ai-virtual-receptionist-voice) covers off-script handling and transfers, including one tool that disables call transfers in after-hours-only mode.


## Outbound sales and lead qualification


The agent works a lead list: it confirms it has the right person, asks a few qualifying questions, then books a meeting or passes a warm lead to a rep.


Outbound adds problems inbound does not have. The agent speaks first, so the opening line and the AI disclosure have to be right before the human says anything. Answering-machine detection comes next: within the first few seconds the agent decides between human and voicemail, and a wrong call either pitches a recording or hangs up on a person. Opt-outs are the third check, since a caller who says "stop calling" mid-pitch has to end the call and leave the list. For the test plan, see[how to test an outbound voice agent before the campaign dials](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/outbound-voice-ai-qa) .


## Banking servicing


The agent authenticates the caller, then handles balance lookups, card locks, payments and dispute intake. Fraud alerts run outbound: the agent calls after a risk engine trips, confirms whether the cardholder made the transaction, and locks the card if not. Our[fintech voice agent testing guide](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/voice-bot-testing-fintech) covers how to test that flow.


Identifiers are the failure that matters. In a University of Sheffield study of spoken serial numbers, a recognizer scoring 96.6% on individual characters got 77% of complete identifiers right, close to one in four wrong. The study used British English serial numbers, so measure your own line. The second failure is a partial write: the agent says the card is locked while the tool call returned an error. Assert on the tool payload and read values back before anything moves money. Our guide to[banking voice agents](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/voicebot-in-banking) covers seven call types and the accuracy bar for each.


## Insurance claims and policy servicing


The agent takes first notice of loss (date, location, parties, damage), answers claim status questions, and processes policy changes such as adding a financed vehicle.


The adjuster inherits everything captured on that call. A wrong date of loss can put a covered event outside the policy period, and a VIN runs 17 characters with no room for a near miss. Turn detection fails quietly: a caller pauses to read a policy number off a card, the agent treats the pause as the end of the turn, and it answers half a number. The agent also needs a hard boundary on coverage: it reports claim status and routes settlement decisions to a licensed adjuster. The[guide to conversational AI in insurance](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/conversational-ai-in-insurance) maps each use case to the obligations its call carries.


## Collections and payment reminders


The agent places outbound calls to confirm it has reached the right party, delivers the required disclosures, then takes a payment or logs a[promise to pay](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/conversational-ai-in-banking) . Payment reminders are the lighter version of the same flow.


The obligations are the hard part. The debt disclosure has to land at the right moment, the agent must not discuss the account until the right person is verified, and a wrong-party call has to end without exposing a balance. Amounts and dates break next: one wrong digit moves the wrong sum, and fixing it takes a person and another call. Opt-outs and calling windows need scenarios of their own. Score each disclosure at the step that owes it, because one score across a long call hides which duty went missing.


## Logistics dispatch and delivery confirmation


The agent calls drivers and carriers to confirm pickup and delivery windows, collects ETAs, and writes status into the transport or fleet system. Drivers also call in for dock numbers and changed appointments.


Noise breaks it first. Cab audio and road noise degrade STT where load numbers and street addresses have to be exact, and drivers talk over the agent, so interruption handling and VAD tuning matter more than on an office line. Integration is the second break: the call only has value if the ETA lands in the fleet platform, and complex fleet systems return partial data, time out, or disagree with what the driver said. Add a fast escalation rule for drivers who report a delay or damage, and test it on your noisiest audio.


## How to tell a use case is ready for production


Cekura organizes testing into five areas, and each answers a different readiness question.


- **Workflow simulations:** run[end-to-end simulations](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/voice-ai-simulation) of the full call type, including branches where the caller changes their mind, and evaluate each against a written success condition such as "the appointment exists at the requested time".
- **Repeat runs:** run each scenario at least three times and count it as passing only when every run passes.
- **Infrastructure testing:** replay interruptions, background noise, long pauses and added latency, because VAD and STT behave differently on a noisy line than in a quiet test.
- **Production call monitoring:** evaluate live calls against the same rubric as the pre-launch tests, and turn failed calls into regression scenarios.
- **Red teaming:** probe identity checks and scope limits with[adversarial callers](https://www.cekura.ai/blogs/ai-red-teaming) who attempt social engineering or ask for advice the agent must not give.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the most common voice AI use cases?


Appointment scheduling, inbound support with call deflection, virtual receptionist and routing, outbound sales qualification, and servicing calls in banking and insurance. Healthcare intake, collections and delivery confirmation are common too. They share a profile: the caller's goal is specific, and the agent can reach the system that completes it.


### Which voice AI use cases are hardest to automate?


Calls with the most obligations per minute and the least tolerance for a wrong digit: collections, disputes, claims intake, and any call carrying protected health information. Each needs verified identity, disclosures at the right moment and exact capture of numbers. Triage and any call that ends in advice or a settlement decision stay partly human.


### How do you test a voice AI use case before launch?


Run end-to-end simulations of the call type, including interruptions, noise and callers who change their minds, and evaluate each against a written success condition. Repeat each scenario several times, since one pass proves only that the path exists. Add adversarial callers for the verification step, then evaluate live calls on the same rubric after launch.
